## Natural history notes

A tiny plant bug characterized by a slender pale green to yellowish body, long legs, and quick jumping or hopping movements when disturbed. In Florida, the Cotton Fleahopper is found in fields, roadsides, gardens, weedy edges, and agricultural areas where cotton, hibiscus, mallow, and other herbaceous host plants occur. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing tender plant tissue, buds, and flowers, sometimes damaging cotton squares and other developing plant parts, while also serving as prey for spiders, assassin bugs, lacewings, birds, and parasitoid wasps.
